_comment: Maintainer's judgment, not ArenaNet's. Two axes: conduct (show info vs prompt action) and advantage (how much edge it confers). Every entry non-none on either axis MUST carry an `evidence` string quoted verbatim from that repo's own catalog description or one of its topics - tests/conduct-data.test.mjs enforces it. Scope: repos carrying the `injection` signal, plus anything added by hand.

qq1ng/rezzOrder.rationale: Reads squad state and tells the player when to act, rather than showing state and leaving the decision to them. The information itself is already on screen; what the addon adds is the instruction.
qq1ng/rezzOrder.evidence: shows whose turn it is to rez

CopraCoperal/Guild-Wars-2-Hellstorm.rationale: Advertises itself on competitive edge rather than on any function, and its own topic list names bots, ESP, noclip, radar, speedhack and teleport. Nothing here assists a player's own play; it substitutes for it.
CopraCoperal/Guild-Wars-2-Hellstorm.evidence: give you an edge over your competitors

BasaltRobinSky/guild-wars-2-trainer.rationale: A trainer removes the constraints play is made of. Invulnerability, movement speed and cooldowns are not information the player acts on - they are the mechanics the encounter consists of, suspended.
BasaltRobinSky/guild-wars-2-trainer.evidence: god mode, infinite health, unlimited gold, teleport, speed hack, and instant skill cooldown

Coredelprotect/guild-wars-2-trainer.rationale: Same class as any other trainer: the listed features suspend the mechanics rather than inform the player about them. The educational-purposes disclaimer does not change what the described software does.
Coredelprotect/guild-wars-2-trainer.evidence: god mode, unlimited money, cooldown hacks

nika-qubit/Gamma.rationale: Macro tools execute input sequences on the player's behalf, which is acting rather than informing. The quantitative-analysis half would be assistive on its own; the macro half is what sets the tier.
nika-qubit/Gamma.evidence: Quantitative Analysis Platform and Macro Tools

kxtools/kx-vision.rationale: Shows rather than instructs, so conduct stays assistive - but ESP draws player positions the client deliberately occludes, and a gear inspector reads builds the game does not expose. This is the axis-independence case: it issues no order and still confers a decisive edge.

x4c1/arcdps_esp.rationale: A client-side minimap built on arcdps draws positional information into the client. The description is too thin to support a stronger claim than that, so the grade stops at some - the repository name suggests more, but a name is not evidence.

husnaintariq577/kx-vision.rationale: Carries the kx-vision name but claims only a real-time data overlay in its own words. Graded on what this description actually says rather than on what the upstream project does.

FrostyInk/Boonvision-Release.rationale: Recoloring boons and auras amplifies perception: it makes effects easier to tell apart than the unmodified client presents them. No instruction is issued, so conduct stays assistive.

TMcBoyle/GW2-mechanic-timer.rationale: Surfaces encounter mechanic timing as a countdown the game does not display. It shows state and leaves the decision to the player, but the state itself is not otherwise available.

TaimiHUD/TaimiHUD.rationale: Encounter timers and pathing render information the client does not present natively. Markers and pathing are long-tolerated in practice, which is why this grades as some rather than strong.

mriot/prep-alert.rationale: Reminds the player about food and utility buffs, but every buff still costs the player their own click - one action per one click, which is the line ArenaNet actually draws. A reminder that leaves both the decision and the keypress with the player is assistive, and the buffs are available to everyone, so no advantage attaches.

fodaveg/tyrian-companion-nexus.rationale: Surfaces loot and trading post prices the player would otherwise look up manually. An alert is a notification, not an input: the player still opens the trading post and clicks every buy themselves. The prices are public through the official API, so no advantage attaches either.
fodaveg/tyrian-companion-nexus.evidence: loot and price alerts inside the game

fodaveg/tyrian-companion-blish.rationale: The Blish HUD build of the same tool, assessed on the same terms: it notifies, and the player still performs every action by hand. The prices come from the official public API.
fodaveg/tyrian-companion-blish.evidence: loot and price alerts over the game

Stukeley/Gw2TpPriceChecker.rationale: Watches public trading post prices and notifies at a threshold the player set. It runs outside the client and cannot act in it - every trade is the player's own click - so it reports rather than plays.
Stukeley/Gw2TpPriceChecker.evidence: send an alert if the price is below/above set threshold

Taschenbuch/BlishHud-GatheringTools.rationale: Reminds the player at the logout dialog that gathering tools are missing. The state is already visible in the inventory and the module cannot equip anything; it surfaces information at a useful moment and leaves every action to the player.
Taschenbuch/BlishHud-GatheringTools.evidence: shows a reminder in the Logout Dialog

FScaley/GW2-TP-Assistant.rationale: Presents flipping and crafting analysis over public trading post data. It informs a decision the player then makes and executes themselves, one click per action, and the data it reasons over is available to anyone through the official API.

Zerthox/arcdps-food-reminder.rationale: Named a reminder, but by its own description it tracks buff food and utility items - showing state, not prompting an action. Assessed on the description rather than the name.

leonvchan/gw2_birthday_reminder.rationale: Prompts, but not about game state: character birthdays are an account date, and claiming a gift involves no timing decision with a better or worse answer.

jsantorek/GW2-Alerts.rationale: Infrastructure rather than a tool a player reads: it republishes the game's own alerts as Nexus events for other addons to consume. What a consumer does with them is that addon's verdict, not this one's.

stormalize/tempo.rationale: The auto-attack in the name is the game's own attack chain, not automation - this is a Reffect display pack showing where in that chain the player is.

FScaley/GW2-CLE-Timer.rationale: Meta and boss event timers run on a fixed public schedule that is documented on the wiki and visible in-game. Presenting it more conveniently is not an information advantage.

cordbleibaum/ArcDPS-Timer.rationale: A speedrunning timer measures elapsed time after the fact. It reports nothing about game state and prompts nothing.

csh/ReshadeEffectShaderToggler-GW2.rationale: ReShade presets are the class where perception advantage usually lives, but this one's stated purpose is the opposite: excluding the game UI from effects. Nothing in its own words claims added clarity.

Emisan01/Gw2Purgator.rationale: Startup diagnostics and shader cache cleanup act on the installation, not on play. The injection and memory signals are about how it works, not what it is for.

ChrisnNg/GW2-Arcdps-Updater.rationale: Downloads and renames a DLL so arcdps and ReShade can coexist. It is installer plumbing and makes no claim on gameplay.

faker-ino/DrfGoldTracker.rationale: Totals the loot and gold a session produced. Accounting after the fact, with no bearing on a decision in play.

qjv/assisted_deployment_and_departure.rationale: Launches and cleans up companion processes around the game. It never touches gameplay state.

Linkaaaaa/GW2CombatTimer.rationale: Displays time spent in combat, which is a readout of something the player just did rather than information about what to do next.

albrektsson/gw2-session-tracker.rationale: A session tracker summarises what a play session yielded. Its own description claims nothing beyond being a Nexus addon.
